raw_response:
I’ve farmed here a long time, so I won’t change too much unless I have a reason. On my 11.4 mu, I will still keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is my steady income and grain for the household feels safer. But I will leave a smaller piece for cotton, because cotton can still bring cash if the price is decent, and it spreads the risk. I don’t have unlimited money, and some people in the family work off-farm, so labor at the busy times is tight. Because of that, I will not push the inputs to the highest level. I’ll use enough fertilizer to avoid obvious yield loss, irrigate at the key stages with the well, and keep the management simple enough that I can handle it.

For wheat, I trust the usual local calendar. I’ll sow in early October on the land I want to follow with maize, using an improved local variety because saved seed is not as even. I usually put most fertilizer as base, then watch the crop at jointing and give one topdress if the stand looks a little weak or yellow. Wheat is worth protecting because if I save too much on fertilizer and water, the heads come up short and I lose more than I save. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll plant summer maize right away on the same land. That turnaround is always rushed, so I will keep tillage light and use one pass if possible, not heavy plowing. For maize, I don’t want to overspend, but I also know if I starve it early the ears won’t size well, so I’ll still give a base dressing and one topdress around the knee-high stage. Cotton I’ll keep on a smaller area. Cotton takes more watching and more picking labor later, so I won’t plant too much at my age. I’ll fertilize it moderately, irrigate a couple of times if it turns dry, and spray only when insects or weeds really show up.
